thread.title: Boeing, Apple, Caterpillar, Visa, Wal-Mart Are The Top 5 Dow Stocks In 2017

author: GILLIAN RICH
title: Boeing, Apple, Caterpillar, Visa, Wal-Mart Are The Top 5 Dow Stocks In 2017
text:
TheDow Jones industrial average is closing out its best year since 2013 and Boeing ( BA ), Caterpillar ( CAT ), Apple ( AAPL ), Visa ( V ) and Wal-Mart ( WMT ) were the top five blue-chip winners in 2017. All five were big winners in the broader S&P 500 index as well.
Boeing X Boeing was the overall Dow leader, soaring 89.5%, as the aerospace and defense sector heat up.
Demand was strong in the defense and commercial sectors throughout the year and Boeing ramped up production rates of its 787 Dreamliner and narrow-body 737 to meet the increasing demand.
Boeing's free cash flow rose as the company found ways to cut production costs and investors got their wish last week, when Boeing announced an $18 billion repurchase program and a 20% dividend hike to $1.71.
Caterpillar Caterpillar climbed 71% in 2017. The construction and mining equipment maker was the best performer in the past six months, jumping 58.8%, edging past Boeing's 48.6%. Commodities have rebounded, boosting demand for heavy mining equipment, while housing markets in the U.S. and China remain strong.
 
Visa Visa rose 46.45% in 2017, moving into third place on the final trading day of the year. The credit-card network provider is riding strong consumer sentiment as more jobs are created and wages rise. Payment stocks of all stripes have been big winners over the past 12 months.
Visa is well positioned for 2018 as improving economies in Europe could help the company, which acquired Visa Europe last year, along with growth in China, Japan and India.
Apple Apple slipped to fourth place, but gained 46.2% in 2017.
The tech giant released its highly anticipated iPhone X in November, the biggest redesign in three years, along with the cheaper iPhone 8. Looking ahead to 2018, analysts question if the new product releases were enough to spark a "supercycle" of smartphone upgrades.
Wal-Mart Wal-Mart rounds out the top five, rising 43.1% during the year. The discounter took on Amazon ( AMZN ) by improving its e-commerce offerings with its purchase of Jet.com and Shoebuy.com in 2016, vintage millennial brand ModCloth and high-end outdoor gear site Moosejaw in 2017. The company also bought Parcel, a same-day grocery and meal kit delivery service, in October.
Wal-Mart's online sales boomed in 2017, with U.S. same-store sales climbing, restoring confidence that the world's largest retailer will not only survive but thrive going forward.
The discounter is looking at other ways to take on Amazon, with Wal-Mart reportedly developing a cashier-less store to take on Amazon Go, a test store in Seattle that uses computer vision to facilitate check outs.
